title: How Twitter Built Your Timeline: Fan-Out Explained #Shorts
shortTitle: How Twitter Built Your Timeline — DDIA Chapter 1 Short
book: Martin Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications (O'Reilly, 1st edition, 2017)

description.summary: Around 2012, Twitter served about 300,000 timeline reads a second but only about 4,600 new tweets a second. Here is how that pushed them from fan-out on read to fan-out on write, why accounts with over 30 million followers broke the simple version, and the hybrid that fixed it. From Chapter 1 of Designing Data-Intensive Applications.
figureNotes: Twitter numbers are historical figures from around 2012, as cited in the book (4,600 tweets/s on average, over 12,000 at peak; 300,000 timeline reads/s; 75 followers per tweet on average; some accounts with over 30 million followers).
